quote: It’s a high-entropy state into which the system trends, an attractor in human psychology.
content: The thermodynamic metaphor is asserted, and the sociology of organizations describes a different default. The documented trajectory of causes and movements is routinization, Weber's term for the conversion of charismatic enthusiasm into bureaucracy, followed by moderation, institutional capture and decline; the social-movement literature finds that most movements do not intensify but professionalize and fade. High-commitment groups are the minority, and they are produced by specific conditions, strict demands, exit costs, isolation, that most causes never acquire (Iannaccone 1994). The essay's claim is also unfalsifiable as stated: every group that fails to become a cult was "pumping against entropy," and every group that does was not, so no observation can count against the attractor. A metaphor from physics is doing the work of a finding, in an essay that says the worthiness of a cause does not excuse its adherents from measuring.

quote: Every group of people with an unusual goal—good, bad, or silly—will trend toward the cult attractor unless they make a constant effort to resist it.
content: The prediction has since been tested on its author's own movement, and the result is instructive either way. The rationalist community that grew from these essays made the constant effort the essay prescribes, with explicit norms against guru-worship and a genre of self-critical writing that this essay founded, and it has nonetheless been the subject of repeated accounts, from former members and from journalists, of groups within and adjacent to it exhibiting the isolation, leader-centering and dissent-suppression the essay describes, in at least one offshoot ending in deaths. That is not a refutation of the essay, which predicted exactly this risk. It is evidence about the remedy: the effort the essay says is sufficient was made, at length and in public, and did not prevent the outcome in the cases where the other risk factors, charismatic leadership, total worldview, communal living, were present. The essay's heat-pump needed a specification of what the pump actually does, and "constant effort" is not one.
